articles.title: Women at the controls, solar power on the rooftops: What makes Pune Metro's Pink Line special
articles.summary: On November 3, Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for Pune Metro projects worth around Rs 21,800 crore.
articles.body: On November 3, Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for Pune Metro projects worth around Rs 21,800 crore.The project he inaugurated was Line 3 of Pune Metro, popularly known as the Pink Line. Built at a cost of approximately Rs 8,300 crore, the 23.2-km corridor connects Maan, on Pune's northwestern outskirts, with the District Court Metro station in Shivajinagar, central Pune. Also known as Civil Court station, it serves as an interchange with Line 1 (Purple Line) and Line 2 (Aqua Line), connecting passengers to other parts of the Metro network.PM Modi described the Pink Line as "so special". Beyond the connectivity it offers, the corridor stands out for its distinctive approach to operations, infrastructure development and sustainability.Why Pune needed the MetroOver the years, Pune's population has grown significantly, with people from other parts of Maharashtra as well as outside the state migrating to the city. Pune was home to over 12 lakh people in 1981, according to that year's national census. The figure rose to more than 31 lakh in 2011, the latest national census, meaning the city added around 19 lakh people in 30 years – an increase of nearly 160%.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();Migration to Pune and the subsequent population expansion have largely been driven by the growth of its IT, manufacturing and educational sectors. Pune is counted among India's leading IT hubs, alongside Bengaluru and Hyderabad. Several prominent colleges and universities are also located in the city, further contributing to its growing population and demand for public transport.Against this backdrop, the foundation stone for the first phase of Pune Metro, comprising the Purple and Aqua lines, was laid in December 2016. The network's commercial operations commenced in March 2022.Although the launch of Pune Metro improved connectivity, several important areas remained outside its network, limiting its reach. The Pink Line addresses part of this gap by connecting Hinjawadi to the existing Metro network.Why the Pink Line mattersThe significance of the Pink Line extends beyond it being just another corridor of the Pune Metro network. Before the route opened to the public on November 4, a day after its inauguration, the network had no connectivity to Hinjawadi, one of Pune's largest employment centres and a major IT hub. The area houses offices of major technology companies such as Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services, Wipro and Cognizant.The Purple Line, which runs between Pimpri-Chinchwad and Swargate, and the Aqua Line, connecting Vanaz and Ramwadi, were the only two operational corridors at the time. As a result, software professionals living in other parts of Pune had to rely on road transport to commute to Hinjawadi or relocate closer to their workplaces.With 17 of the corridor's stations now operational and the remaining six scheduled to open in March 2027, commuters can interchange at District Court station in Shivajinagar and travel directly to Hinjawadi, making daily commutes more seamless.Commuters have also expressed hope that the Pink Line will ease congestion on roads leading to Hinjawadi.“The entire stretch from Wakad to Hinjawadi Phase-II remains busy and chaotic during rush hours. We expect relief from these snarls,” a commuter told The Times of India in an earlier report.Another commuter, who travels by bike to his workplace at Balewadi near Hinjawadi, noted that the Metro journey took nearly as much time as his two-wheeler commute but offered greater comfort.“My travel time by bike would be around 30-45 minutes, depending on the traffic. It took about 30 minutes to reach Balewadi by Metro. There was no huge drop in the travel time, but the overall comfort in Metro was much more,” he added.Another important feature of the Pink Line, officials say, is its provision for last-mile connectivity through bus services, dedicated pickup zones for taxis and auto-rickshaws, and cycle parking at stations.With the Pink Line now open, the Aqua and Purple lines being expanded, and a fourth corridor taking shape, the focus will increasingly be on integrating the expanding Metro network with other transport modes to improve connectivity across Pune.Women at the controlsIn October 2011, a woman loco pilot, Priyanka N, drove the inaugural train of Namma Metro in Bengaluru. Since then, several Metro networks across the country have employed women as train operators.However, Pune has taken this a step further by introducing an entire Metro corridor where all train drivers are women.While other Metro networks in India, including Delhi and Bengaluru, also have corridors designated as the Pink Line, Pune's newest Metro corridor has a special significance attached to the name. Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis said the corridor would be called the Pink Line because its trains would be operated exclusively by women.Nearly 15 years after Priyanka N drove the first Namma Metro train, Pune Metro's Pink Line has become India's first Metro corridor to have an all-women team of train drivers.As many as 90 women have completed training and obtained competency certificates to operate trains on the Hinjawadi–Shivajinagar route. Recruited through campus drives, they underwent classroom instruction, practical sessions and extensive on-track training before being cleared to operate passenger services. The women have since taken charge of regular train operations on the corridor.Overall, the plan is to have 100 women operators on the line, including the 90 already operating trains on it.Having an entire Metro corridor with women at the controls also marks a significant step towards greater representation of women in operational roles in urban rail transport.A Metro corridor powered partly by solar energyAnother important feature of Pune Metro's Pink Line is that 30% of its energy requirements are expected to be met through solar power. The project also uses a 750V DC third-rail electrification system, which eliminates the need for overhead wires.Tata Power Renewables has received a contract from Pune IT City Metro Rail Ltd, which operates Pune Metro Line 3, to install a 7.67 MWp rooftop solar project. The installation will cover all 23 stations and the Metro depot. The electricity generated will be used for captive consumption. The project is expected to help reduce the corridor's operating costs and dependence on conventional sources of electricity.With this, Pune Metro joins several transport projects in India, including other Metro systems, that use solar power. For instance, as of 2023, 35% of Delhi Metro's total energy consumption came from renewable sources. This included 30% from its off-site solar power plant in Rewa, Madhya Pradesh, 4% from rooftop solar panels and 1% from the waste-to-energy plant in Ghazipur, Delhi.Outside the Metro network, Cochin International Airport in Kerala became the world's first airport to run entirely on solar power with the commissioning of a 12 MWp solar PV power plant in 2015.The solar power component, therefore, adds another dimension to the Pink Line's approach to energy use and operational efficiency.India's first Metro project under the 2017 Metro policy's PPP frameworkThe Pink Line is also significant for the model through which it has been developed. It is India's first Metro rail project to be implemented under the public-private partnership (PPP) framework of the Centre's New Metro Rail Policy, 2017, which aims to encourage private investment in transport infrastructure.While cities such as Mumbai and Hyderabad have previously developed Metro projects under PPP models, Pune's Pink Line is the first to be implemented under the framework of the 2017 policy.The project was developed by Pune IT City Metro Rail Limited, a special-purpose company established as a joint venture between TRIL Urban Transport Private Limited, part of the Tata Group, and Germany's Siemens, in collaboration with the Pune Metropolitan Region Development Authority.Another technological feature of the Pink Line is its Siemens-supplied Communication-Based Train Control (CBTC) signalling system. While the existing Purple and Aqua lines also use CBTC systems, these are supplied by France's Alstom.According to Siemens, its CBTC system allows trains to communicate continuously with trackside equipment, enabling high-frequency services while maintaining safe distances between trains. It is designed for semi-automated operations, with provision for a future upgrade to fully automated, driverless operations.The technology adds to the corridor's operational capabilities while leaving scope for greater automation in the future.Beyond Metro connectivityDespite these features and the integration of Hinjawadi into the Metro network, several challenges remain in improving the overall commuting experience in the city, experts say.For instance, despite the Pink Line reportedly recording a ridership of around 50,000 on its very first day, some passengers raised concerns about gaps in first- and last-mile connectivity.According to Tanzeel Allapur, programme associate at Parisar, a Pune-based NGO working on sustainable urban transport since 1995, the administration cannot limit its idea of a good commuting experience to building new Metro lines alone and must focus on improving connectivity to and from Metro stations.“Finding a connecting bus or shared auto, figuring out where to board, and navigating the surroundings of a Metro station all add to the mental effort involved in making that journey. The administration needs to focus on reducing both the physical friction and the cognitive load involved in these transfers,” she told The Times of India.Echoing this view, Jagannarayan Padmanabhan, senior director at Crisil Intelligence, stressed the importance of seamless connectivity rather than simply adding more routes.“Seamless connectivity with PMPML buses, feeder services, autos and shared mobility, supported by integrated ticketing and pedestrian infrastructure, is essential,” he added.Although it is still early days for the Pink Line, improved connectivity and integration with other modes of transport could further build on the benefits it brings to Pune's public transport network.The way forward for Pune Metro's Pink LineLooking ahead, transport activist Ranjit Gadgil, who heads Parisar, said that with the Pink Line now operational alongside the two existing corridors, authorities must introduce measures to curb private vehicle use to reduce congestion, pollution and road accidents.“With the addition of the Pink Line to the existing two corridors, it is high time the city started implementing measures to curb vehicle use. These could include on-street parking charges, low-emission zones and street designs that prioritise the safety and movement of pedestrians, cyclists and buses rather than allocating more space to motor vehicles,” he added.Ultimately, the Pink Line offers Pune an opportunity to make public transport a more convenient choice for commuters. Its connectivity to Hinjawadi, in particular, could encourage more people working in the IT hub to consider the Metro for their daily journeys.But the real measure of the Pink Line's success will be whether it can persuade more people to leave their cars and two-wheelers behind and make public transport their preferred choice.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: French President Macron gets a frosty reception as Iceland PM appears to dodge his hug in awkward greeting
articles.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron appeared to go in for a hug with Icelandic Prime Minister Kristrún Frostadóttir in Dublin, but she seemed to step back,
articles.body: French President Emmanuel Macron appeared to go in for a hug with Icelandic Prime Minister Kristrún Frostadóttir in Dublin, but she seemed to step back, leaving him leaning in for an awkward greeting.The French president was pictured leaning towards Frostadóttir, who moved back while keeping a hand on his shoulder. She appeared uncomfortable and glanced towards a photographer standing nearby, who captured the exchange.Macron, meanwhile, seemed unfazed, smiling as he looked at her while leaning in to greet her.The encounter took place during a round-table meeting of European leaders at the European Political Community gathering in Dublin, The Daily Mail reported.This is not the first time Macron's public interactions with a woman leader have attracted attention online. His exchanges with Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni have repeatedly sparked discussion on social media.At last year's G7 Summit in Canada's Kananaskis, a video showed Macron leaning towards Meloni and whispering something in her ear.Meloni, who was seated beside him, leaned in to listen before rolling her eyes. The clip went viral, with social media users speculating about what the French president had said.Another interaction between the two leaders drew attention when Macron shook Meloni's hand and kissed it. Her reaction was interpreted by some as displeasure, with reports describing her as looking "furious".The exchange came days after the two leaders had clashed over the inclusion of specific language on abortion rights in the final statement of the June 2024 G7 Summit, hosted by Italy.Another greeting at the Elysee Palace in Paris earlier this year also became a talking point. Macron appeared to prolong a cheek-to-cheek greeting, while Meloni's brief reaction was interpreted by some viewers as one of surprise.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: 'I'm not gonna be cowered': US Treasury chief on moving to military base over Iran threats
articles.summary: Washington's economic war on Iran may be beginning to bite Tehran, but the man spearheading the campaign is now facing a backlash of his own.
articles.body: Washington's economic war on Iran may be beginning to bite Tehran, but the man spearheading the campaign is now facing a backlash of his own.US treasury secretary Scott Bessent has revealed that he was forced to move from his Washington residence to a military base following death threats linked to Iran.But Bessent is refusing to be intimidated, arguing that the threats against him and other senior US officials show that President Donald Trump's financial squeeze on Tehran is working.His message to Iran's leadership was blunt: "F the Iranian leadership. I'm not gonna be cowered."Speaking during an interview with CNBC, Bessent said the threats were directed not only at him but also at other members of Trump's cabinet. He linked the threats to Washington's economic offensive against Tehran, dubbed "Operation Economic Outcast", arguing that the campaign was beginning to hurt Iran.Describing the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as increasingly desperate under mounting economic pressure, Bessent compared its actions to those of a "dangerous cornered animal".He also said he saw no reason to be intimidated when American military personnel stationed in the Gulf and President Donald Trump himself continued to face death threats."And, you know, why am I gonna be afraid when our brave military personnel in the Gulf, President Trump constantly receives death threats? And, you know, what we are doing is working, and the IRGC, they're like a dangerous cornered animal," he said.Bessent has led the Trump administration's economic pressure campaign against Iran since August. According to Reuters, Operation Economic Outcast involves sanctions targeting financial institutions and services in the Middle East that facilitate transactions with Tehran. The campaign, combined with a US naval blockade of Iranian ports, is aimed at pressuring Iran to end attacks on shipping and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.The security concerns come amid broader US intelligence warnings about Iranian targeting efforts. A senior intelligence official in the Trump administration warned in a memo seen by Reuters last month that Iranian plots against US personnel and American citizens had reached an "advanced stage".Bessent also accused The Wall Street Journal of compromising his security by publishing an aerial photograph of his Georgetown residence in January 2025, which he said contained information that made the property geolocatable. He claimed his team had appealed to the newspaper's editor not to disclose the location."So, I follow the Secret Service instructions and have moved from my home to a military base," Bessent told CNBC, before describing the newspaper's decision as "highly irresponsible and dangerous".Trump, meanwhile, issued a fresh warning to Tehran, saying those responsible for killing a US official "will not exist any longer". In a phone interview with Salem News Channel, the US president was asked how Washington would respond if Iran targeted an American official, including Bessent.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2016, Boston construction crews uncovered a burned 19th-century ship beneath the Seaport; its abandoned lime cargo linked the wreck to the city’s building boom
articles.summary: In 2016, construction crews uncovered a burned 19th-century ship beneath Boston's Seaport District, revealing its lime cargo that links to the city's historic building boom in the 19th century.
articles.body: Boston Seaport District was once part of a busy harbour, where ships transported materials that supported the growth. Much of that maritime history now lies beneath modern buildings. According to Content Boston, in May 2016, construction workers uncovered a burnt wooden vessel while preparing the foundation for a new office building. The ship still contained partially burnt barrels of lime, offering clues about the trade that supplied Boston's expanding construction industry during the 19th century.Construction work exposed the buried schooner The site of the find was located at 121 Seaport Boulevard during the process of excavating the building's foundation. The spot used to be part of South Boston Flats, a mud flat covered with water that was gradually turned into land. According to the City of Boston Archaeology Program, the wooden hull lay under 20 feet of fill when two H-piles driven in during construction struck the wreck. Skanska halted construction work at the site and hired the Public Archaeology Laboratory (PAL) to investigate the discovery. Assistance in the research was provided by archaeologists from the city of Boston, the Massachusetts Historical Commission, the Board of Underwater Archaeological Resources and David S. Robinson and Associates.According to the City of Boston Archaeology Program, the surviving hull measured 47 feet long and 15 feet wide. Its stem was missing, but archaeologists estimated that the original vessel was between 60 and 80 feet long. Two mast steps indicated that it was a two-masted schooner, likely a type known as a pinky. The City of Boston archaeological report documents these findings.Lime barrel pointed to a possible Rockland connectionArchaeologists discovered dozens of partially burned wooden barrels filled with lime. They were roughly 1.5 to 2.5 feet in size and bound together with natural birch hoops. The partially visible stencil “ROCKLA” on the barrel lead indicated that the lime shipment came from Rockland, Maine, one of the principal centres of lime production in the mid to late 19th century.Lime was an essential component of the mortar required in the masonry construction process. Boston required a lot of time in the development of its Financial District, Back Bay, Beacon Hill and South End Neighbourhoods. This cargo may indicate a link between the schooner and the city's construction activities. According to the City of Boston, historical records of a similar-sized lime schooner documented a cargo of more than 1,200 barrels of lime. Archaeologists believe the Seaport Shipwreck may have carried a similar load.West lime may have contributed to the ship's destructionFire seems to have been a major factor in the sinking of the ship because of all the blackened areas on its hull and cargo. This is based on the fact that lime reacts exothermically when in contact with water, releasing heat in the process. As for the exact cause of the fire, it still remains unknown. One piece of evidence that can help explain this mystery is the orientation of the ship. This is because the bow of the ship faces northeast and seems to indicate that it had been out to the South Boston Flats and left there intentionally. The Massachusetts Board of Underwater Archaeological Resources’ minutes from its May 26, 2016 meeting also recorded the discovery and described the vessel as a likely lime schooner that burned and was abandoned at the site.Artifacts helped narrow down the sinking periodHousehold items that were found included ironstone dishes, a knife, a tobacco pipe made from clay and two three-tinned forks. The three-tinned forks proved to be especially helpful since the design was invented in 1869. The City of Boston notes that the site began to be filled in 1885, which places the sinking somewhere between 1869 and 1885. When considered alongside evidence dating the wreck to no earlier than 1869, this places its sinking between 1869 and 1885. The name of the ship is unknown and it seems that it was built at the beginning of the 19th century, judging by the compass timbers on board.Archaeologists documented the risk before its removalThe removal of the ship took place after it was documented and divided into several large pieces to allow work to proceed on site. Flatbed trucks were used to transport the remains to be studied later. There were 13 archival pieces, which included parts of the ship's keel, hull planking and barrels. The Massachusetts Board's archaeological records provide further context about the state’s work to document and protect maritime heritage. The Boston discovery preserved a record of the trade that supported the city‘s growth, even though the schooner's identity and exact fate remain unresolved.You use AI every day. articles.title: A $25,000 grant from Microsoft cofounder Paul Allen's family foundation helped keep a historic Washington art gallery open in 2025; it has now received a third grant as 745 arts groups share $10 million
articles.summary: A $25,000 grant from the family foundation of Microsoft cofounder Paul Allen helped keep the Old Hotel Art Gallery in Othello, Washington, open during a
articles.body: A $25,000 grant from the family foundation of Microsoft cofounder Paul Allen helped keep the Old Hotel Art Gallery in Othello, Washington, open during a difficult stretch in 2025, according to ArtsFund’s 2026 Community Accelerator Grantee announcement. The gallery has now received a third $25,000 grant, part of a broader $10 million distribution to 745 arts and culture organisations across Washington state, as reported by GeekWire and ArtsFund.The funding is not tied to a specific project, which gives smaller organisations the flexibility to pay staff, cover rent, improve buildings, or sustain programming. For the Old Hotel Art Gallery, that flexibility proved decisive, allowing it to bridge a financial gap and continue serving its community. Read more about it here, as per the reports:A gallery with a historyThe Old Hotel Art Gallery is located in Othello, a city in Adams County in central Washington. It operates from a historic building that has become an important cultural space for the surrounding community, offering exhibitions and arts programming in an area that can be easily overlooked by larger arts funders.The gallery received $25,000 grants in each of 2024, 2025, and 2026 through the Community Accelerator Grant program. That consistency has allowed the organisation to plan beyond a single year rather than constantly scrambling to cover basic operating costs.Gallery director Samantha Copas said, as per ArtsFund, that the 2025 award “truly kept our doors open.” The funding helped the gallery support a living wage for staff, bridge a gap until its annual fundraiser, and make improvements and renovations to the historic building.What the money made possibleThe grant did more than prevent a closure. It enabled the Old Hotel Art Gallery to invest in its building, which opened the door to a new revenue stream through rental income. That kind of practical investment can change an organisation’s financial outlook over time.For many small arts groups, the difference between surviving and closing often comes down to a few months of cash flow. A grant that covers payroll, rent, or facility repairs can buy time for an organisation to stabilise and continue its work.The Old Hotel Art Gallery’s experience shows how unrestricted funding can have a multiplier effect. Money used to improve a building can create rental income, which can then support staff, programming, and future operations.A statewide funding effortThe 2026 Community Accelerator Grant awarded $10 million to 745 arts and culture organisations across Washington. Grants ranged from $2,500 to $25,000, reaching organisations in 37 of the state’s 39 counties, as per the reports.The program is administered by ArtsFund and funded by Allen Family Philanthropies, formerly known as the Paul G. Allen Family Foundation. It was created to provide flexible, unrestricted funding to cultural nonprofits whose primary mission is to produce or support arts and cultural activities. The 2026 round focused on organisations with annual budgets under $1 million. That change narrowed the applicant pool but increased the average award size by about 25 percent, from $10,753 in 2025 to $13,423 in 2026.Why small organisations matterThe decision to focus on smaller organisations reflects a broader concern about the health of Washington’s creative sector. According to ArtsFund, organisations with annual budgets under $1 million lost an average of one staff position between 2023 and 2024, while larger organisations added an average of five.That imbalance matters because small groups often serve communities that larger institutions cannot reach as easily. They may be the only arts organisation in a rural county, the only venue for local artists, or the only place where residents can access cultural programming close to home.More than 22 percent of the 2026 grantees are located in rural counties, and the program includes 12 of Washington’s 29 federally recognised tribes. The reach of the funding is therefore not just about dollars, it is about making sure cultural life is supported across the entire state.How the money is usedAlthough the grants are unrestricted, applicants are asked to prioritise how they will use the funds. In 2026, the leading uses cited by grantees were programming, salaries and labour, and rent, mortgage, and facility upgrades.That order makes sense for organisations trying to stay afloat. Programming keeps audiences engaged, salaries keep staff in place, and facility costs determine whether an organisation can physically operate at all.The program also keeps reporting requirements low, with no formal reporting required from grantees. That approach reduces administrative burden and allows organisations to spend more time on their work rather than on paperwork.A commitment to continueArtsFund and Allen Family Philanthropies have also announced a renewal of the Community Accelerator Grant for 2027, unlocking another $10 million for Washington’s arts and culture sector. That brings the program’s total funding to $50 million over five years.The renewal follows a report analysing data from the first three years of the program. It found that 84 percent of organisations that received funding across all three years increased investment in staff, expanded programming, and diversified revenue.Those findings suggest that the grants are doing more than providing short-term relief. They are helping organisations build capacity and resilience, which is especially important in a sector where funding can be unpredictable.What it means for communitiesFor places like Othello, the value of a grant like this goes beyond the gallery itself. It supports jobs, brings people together, gives local artists a platform, and helps preserve a historic building that might otherwise deteriorate.The Old Hotel Art Gallery’s story is a reminder that cultural institutions do not need to be large to be essential. Sometimes, a $25,000 grant is enough to keep the lights on, pay staff, repair a roof, and make sure a community continues to have a place where art and creativity can thrive.As the program enters its fifth year, the challenge will be sustaining that support over time. But the commitment to another $10 million in 2027 suggests that both ArtsFund and Allen Family Philanthropies see the value in continuing to invest in the organisations that keep Washington’s cultural life alive.You use AI every day. articles.title: Watch: CCTV captures chilling moment Brooklyn apartment building collapses, killing 8
articles.summary: A home surveillance camera has captured the terrifying moment a three-storey apartment building in Brooklyn, New York, collapsed, killing eight people and
articles.body: A home surveillance camera has captured the terrifying moment a three-storey apartment building in Brooklyn, New York, collapsed, killing eight people and injuring 18 others.The six-second video shows a family inside their third-floor apartment just moments before the walls give way and debris engulfs the room.The footage, obtained by Gothamist and CBS News, was recorded inside the apartment of resident Anderson Velez at 1321 Flatbush Avenue.Velez lived there with his wife and two young sons. The building collapsed next to an active construction site, prompting authorities to investigate whether work at the site may have contributed to the disaster.At the beginning of the video, Velez's nine-year-old son can be seen taking a gallon of milk from the refrigerator while his two-year-old brother plays on the floor.Their mother then opens the door to the living room and screams. The older boy runs towards her, moving away from the wall just before it collapses. The toddler was swept into the rubble but survived with scrapes to his forehead and legs.Recalling his condition after he was rescued, Velez told Gothamist in Spanish, according to the New York Post: "His ears were full of dirt, his nose, his little mouth, his back, his entire body was covered in dirt."Velez was in the Bronx for work when the building collapsed. He said his wife called him in panic as she pleaded with rescue workers to pull their children from the debris.His wife suffered serious injuries to her ribs, spine and collarbone, while their nine-year-old son remains in intensive care after undergoing surgery.Velez said the family had moved into the apartment earlier this month after living in a homeless shelter. They are now staying at a Brooklyn hotel arranged by the city for people displaced by the collapse.The collapse claimed eight lives, including those of two children aged nine and 10. Two of the deceased were construction workers, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said.Six people died at the scene, while two others succumbed to their injuries at nearby hospitals. The 18 injured included 14 civilians and four firefighters."As of now, we have confirmed that two of those who died were construction workers," Mamdani said while briefing reporters on Thursday. "The vast majority of those still being treated in hospitals are in stable condition. One person is in critical condition," he added.The New York City Fire Department (FDNY) said it had completed search and recovery operations at the site and found no further victims. The site was subsequently handed over to the city's Department of Buildings and Police Department for further investigation.The collapse has raised questions about the building's condition before the accident.You use AI every day. articles.title: State govt forms panel to probe Karnatak University land encroachments
articles.summary: State govt forms panel to verify Karnatak University’s 888-acre land records, trace missing documents and probe alleged encroachment of up to 200 acres.
articles.body: Dharwad: State govt has constituted a committee to verify Karnatak University’s land records and identify alleged encroachments on its property following complaints of large-scale occupation.The committee, headed by the deputy commissioner, will meet on Nov 16 or 17 and submit its report within a month. It includes KU vice-chancellor Prof AM Khan, the tahsildar, commissioners of Hubballi-Dharwad Urban Development Authority and Hubballi-Dharwad Municipal Corporation, and the assistant director of land records.Govt acted after Khan wrote to chief minister’s office seeking intervention to verify the university’s records and reclaim encroached land.Khan said KU, Karnataka’s second-oldest university, owns about 888 acres. Records for nearly 700 acres are available, while documents concerning the remaining 188 acres have yet to be traced and verified.The exercise will examine survey numbers, mutation registers and land records to establish ownership and determine the extent of encroachment. University authorities suspect nearly 200 acres may have been encroached upon over the years, with layouts and permanent structures built on some portions. Preliminary observations have also indicated encroachments along parts of the campus boundary.Accessing and interpreting old records remains a major challenge. Several documents are in Modi script and some in Marathi, requiring translation into Kannada and scrutiny to establish ownership.The exercise is expected to demarcate the university’s boundaries and facilitate measures to recover encroached property.Stay updated with the latest Hubballi news. articles.title: Engineer loses ₹1.3 lakh in credit card KYC scam
articles.summary: Mangaluru cyber fraud cases: engineer, truck driver and retired banker lose ₹1.3 lakh, ₹4.2 lakh and ₹2 lakh in APK, KYC and eChallan scams.
articles.body: Mangaluru: A 47-year-old ship engineer lost Rs 1.3 lakh after cyber fraudsters, posing as bank representatives, allegedly tricked him into sharing his credit card details and downloading APK file under the pretext of updating his KYC details. According to the complaint filed with the CEN police, he received a call on his mobile phone from an unknown number around 3pm on Wednesday. He then shared his credit card details with the caller who claimed to be a bank employee. The caller then told him that a video call was required to update his KYC details and sent him an APK link. When the complainant clicked on the link, a video call was initiated but was disconnected shortly thereafter. Subsequently, a total of Rs 1,36,896 got transferred in multiple transactions from the complainant’s credit card which was now attached to another bank without his knowledge. CEN Crime police registered a case.Truck driver loses ₹4 lakh in fake traffic violation ticketA truck driver, 41, lost Rs 4.2 lakh after cybercriminals allegedly sent him a fake RTO traffic violation message and tricked him into downloading a malicious mobile application. According to the complaint, on Oct 31, around 9.34am, the complainant received a message on his mobile : “Traffic violation CCTV footage pay online”. Along with this, his truck registration number and a link were sent. When he clicked the link, an application named ‘eChallan (mParivahan)’ was allegedly downloaded onto his phone without his knowledge. Subsequently, on Nov 10, he alleged that a total of Rs 4,26,434 was transferred in multiple transactions from his savings bank account to an unknown account without his knowledge. CEN Crime police have registered a case.Pension card scam: Retired bank employee loses ₹2 lakhA 77-year-old retired bank employee lost Rs 2 lakh to a fake Facebook advertisement offering a pension card. According to the complaint, Wednesday, the complainant came across the ad for a ‘retired pension card’. After clicking it, he entered his name, address and PAN card details. At 4.46pm, he received a call from an unidentified person who told him that since he applied online for the pension card, his bank account details were needed to be provided. The complainant shared the information and subsequently, an APK file named ‘Pension card’ was downloaded onto his mobile phone without his knowledge. Later, a total of Rs 2,09,000 was transferred in multiple transactions from his bank account without his knowledge or consent.Stay updated with the latest Mangaluru news. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Trump’s visa restrictions hit Miss Universe: 2 African contestants withdraw, 2 others face uncertainty
articles.summary: Two African contestants have withdrawn from this year's Miss Universe competition in Puerto Rico after failing to secure US visas due to travel
articles.body: Two African contestants have withdrawn from this year's Miss Universe competition in Puerto Rico after failing to secure US visas due to travel restrictions imposed by President Donald Trump's administration. Two other contestants from the continent are also facing uncertainty over their participation as they await visa approvals.According to ABC News, representatives from Zambia and the Republic of Congo have pulled out of the competition after being unable to obtain visas, while contestants from South Sudan and Zimbabwe are still waiting for travel documents.The US has imposed sweeping travel restrictions affecting dozens of countries, including several African nations, through proclamations issued during Trump's second administration. In December last year, the administration expanded the restrictions to include Zambia and Zimbabwe, while maintaining a full suspension of entry for nationals of the Republic of Congo and South Sudan.Miss Universe Zambia organisers announced this week that their representative, Mubanga Pamela Hatyoka, would not be able to participate, saying she deserved the opportunity to represent her country.In the Republic of Congo, Georgina Kambongo, who became the country's first-ever Miss Universe representative, has also been forced to withdraw. National organisers said her inability to travel to Puerto Rico was solely linked to Trump's travel restrictions.Meanwhile, Zimbabwe's representative, Roseanna Hall, said she was still hopeful of securing a visa despite the delays."American visa challenges have delayed that journey, but the fight is not over," Hall said in a social media post, adding that she was not giving up after months of preparation.South Sudan's representative, Adut Deng, also faces an uncertain participation. Organisers said efforts to secure the necessary travel documents and approvals had been underway for months.The 75th edition of Miss Universe is expected to feature up to 120 contestants. Delegates began arriving in Puerto Rico on Sunday for rehearsals and preliminary events.The national costume competition is scheduled for November 21, followed by the swimsuit and evening gown segments on November 22. The winner will be crowned on November 24.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
